statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-70161 is a .NET SDK elevation of privilege issue in workload installation and advertising manifests: an attacker-controlled workload manifest ID can traverse paths under %ProgramData%\dotnet and import attacker-controlled MSBuild targets during elevated workload operations. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the .NET SDK 10.0.1xx feature band as affected from 10.0.100 through 10.0.112 and fixed in 10.0.113, shipped with .NET 10.0.13 (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/453, https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56610, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). The fix makes the cross-platform workload manifest reader reject manifest, workload and pack IDs that are not a single valid path component, and adds Windows-only checks for the elevated installer (the ManifestId check is in the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.113 source tag and not in v10.0.112: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/v10.0.113/src/sdk/src/Resolvers/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WorkloadManifestReader/ManifestId.cs). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, with its Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WorkloadManifestReader.dll, is the SDK of each build's .NET release: SDK 10.0.102 to 10.0.110 in 10.0.2-r0 to 10.0.10-r0, then SDK 10.0.113, 10.0.114 and 10.0.115 in 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0; no 10.0.11 or 10.0.12 build was published for Alpine 3.23. In the x86_64 dotnet10-runtime-artifacts package, the Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WorkloadManifestReader assembly in the 10.0.13-r0 nupkg contains the new path-component check (the ParsePathBasedId and IsValidPathComponent methods). The elevated MSI installer that Microsoft names is not used on Linux, but the manifest reader that carries the fix ships in every build and is used by the SDK's workload commands on Linux, so this is recorded as fixed rather than not affected. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build whose SDK is 10.0.113 or later.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-70161 is a .NET SDK elevation of privilege issue in workload installation and advertising manifests: an attacker-controlled workload manifest ID can traverse paths under %ProgramData%\dotnet and import attacker-controlled MSBuild targets during elevated workload operations. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform, and its list of affected SDKs names only .NET 10 and .NET 11 SDK feature bands; the .NET 9.0.21 release notes also list the CVE (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/453, https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56610, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). The elevated workload operations are those of the MSI-based workload installer: the SDK selects it only for MSI installs and throws an error instead when the operating system is not Windows (https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/v9.0.122/src/Cli/dotnet/commands/dotnet-workload/install/WorkloadInstallerFactory.cs). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every build is a Linux SDK and runtime for x86_64 and aarch64, so dotnet workload commands use the file-based installer and the elevated Windows installer path is never reached in any published build.
